title: The Provision of the Coral Triangle
premise: Lena Brightwater, a desert ranger who has spent a decade outrunning her past one mile at a time, is dragged out of the sand by her old rival, salvage captain Isolde Vane, who holds the deed to a debt Lena can't refuse. Their target: the Coral Triangle, a sunken treasure vessel that carries not gold but a sealed ledger proving Lena's dead mentor betrayed the crew that trusted him — and implicating Lena in what happened the night he died. Racing a rival salvage fleet and the monsoon, six tides at a time, Lena must choose between destroying the truth to protect her mentor's memory and the found family now sailing with her, or surfacing it and losing everything. She raises the ledger, reads it aloud to the crew in the storm's eye, and survives — not because the truth was painless, but because loyalty rebuilt on honesty holds where loyalty built on lies drowned.
about_author: Mara Thornbury is a former marine surveyor who spent seven years charting reef wrecks across the Coral Triangle before turning to fiction. She writes from a houseboat in monsoon season and a landrover in dry season, and claims she can smell a storm three tides out.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Tracking a horse thief across the salt flats, Lena reflects on how she measures time in distance since the night her mentor, Corvin Hale, died. She catches the thief but feels nothing. Beat: hollow competence, the ache of a decade of avoidance.

chapters.title: The Debt in the Sand
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Isolde Vane arrives at the waystation with a signed contract from ten years ago — Lena's mark, a salvage partnership sworn off and never dissolved. The target: the Coral Triangle, lost off the reef coast. Beat: dread and fury at being cornered by her own past.

chapters.title: Sworn Off, Never Broken
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Isolde reveals the rival fleet, led by her former partner Dax Rennard, has the wreck's coordinates and a two-tide head start. She needs Lena's desert-honed tracking eye to read the reef's shifting channels. Beat: reluctant alliance sealed by mutual leverage.

chapters.title: Crew of Strangers
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena meets the crew at the harbor: navigator Pell, a boy who reads currents like scripture; diver Osa, who doesn't speak; engineer Bram, who owes Isolde his life. Lena tests them, they test her back. Beat: guarded first bonds forming over shared distrust.

chapters.title: Six Tides to Monsoon
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. The tide tables give them six tides before the monsoon seals the reef passage for a season. Isolde lays out the race: Rennard's fleet is ahead, the channel behind them closes first. Lena realizes retreat is already impossible. Beat: the trap of commitment, engines turning over.

chapters.title: The Channel of Teeth
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Navigating the reef approach, Lena's desert tracking instincts translate to reading coral and current scars. They pass where Rennard's lead ship grounded and burned. Beat: first proof Lena belongs here, and the first flicker of belonging she didn't ask for.

chapters.title: What the Wreck Was Carrying
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Isolde finally admits the Coral Triangle's cargo isn't treasure — it's Hale's sealed ledger, which Rennard believes names the location of a second, richer wreck. Isolde suspects it names something worse. Beat: the job reframes from salvage to excavation of the past.

chapters.title: Osa's Silence
chapters.summary: Osa's POV, told in near-wordless interiority. Osa dives the wreck's outer hull at slack tide and finds the captain's cabin intact — and a carved mark on the door that matches a scar Osa has carried since childhood. Beat: the past is closer and more personal than anyone knew.

chapters.title: The First Tide Lost
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Rennard's second ship arrives; a boarding skirmish costs them their anchor chain and a full tide. Bram is wounded shielding Pell. Lena makes her first command call under Isolde's eye. Beat: the race turns brutal; the crew stops being strangers.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Lock
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. They recover the sealed strongbox from the captain's cabin, but it's keyed to a mechanism only Hale's hand could open — and Hale is dead. Lena recognizes the lock; she helped him build it. Beat: guilt surfacing; she knows more than she's said.

chapters.title: What Lena Knew
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, confessional. Lena admits to Isolde: Hale built the lock around a secret she once helped hide, the night before the Coral Triangle sailed — and the night he later died was not an accident she witnessed but one she may have caused. Beat: the decade of miles revealed as flight.

chapters.title: Rennard's Offer
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Under a truce flag, Rennard offers Isolde the second wreck's location in exchange for the ledger, claiming it will exonerate them both of an old charge. Isolde is tempted — the charge is hers, not Lena's. Beat: loyalty and self-preservation pulling in opposite directions.

chapters.title: The Broken Tide
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. An uncharted current — the monsoon's outrider — slams the ship onto a coral shelf. Osa dives into collapsing visibility to free the hull. Pell, terrified, holds the line. Beat: the sea takes its toll; Osa is injured; the crew's fear sharpens into resolve.

chapters.title: Hale's Hand
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena opens the lock the only way left: by recreating Hale's technique, muscle memory she buried with him. Inside is the ledger — and a letter addressed to her by name. Beat: the mentor's voice reaching across ten years of silence.

chapters.title: The Letter
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, intimate. The letter reveals Hale knew the Coral Triangle would be scuttled by its own owners to hide the ledger; his death was staged by the same men, and Lena's 'betrayal' the night he died was Hale's own arrangement to save her life. Beat: grief inverted — the memory she fled was a lie built to protect her, and it imprisoned her anyway.

chapters.title: The Storm Makes Landfall
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The monsoon hits early, two tides ahead of schedule. Rennard's fleet is wrecked on the outer reef; his surviving crew begs rescue. Isolde must choose between the race and the people in the water. Beat: survival versus victory — the book's central question made literal.

chapters.title: The Rescue at Rennard's Reef
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. They pull Rennard's people from the sea at the cost of the safe window; the Coral Triangle's passage closes behind them with the ledger still unopened to the world. Rennard, half-drowned, curses them for saving him. Beat: Isolde chooses crew over prize; the fleet becomes a single ship of survivors.

chapters.title: Reading the Ledger
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Sheltering in a sea cave, the crew reads the ledger aloud: names of the owners who scuttled the ship, the sailors written off as lost, Osa's family among them. Isolde's old charge is cleared by the same pages that condemn others. Beat: truth as both wound and absolution.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena must decide: publish the ledger and destroy the shipping families whose patronage keeps Isolde's fleet afloat, or bury it and keep the crew safe and the lie alive. Isolde refuses to decide for her. Beat: the price of survival made explicit; Lena stops running.

chapters.title: The Choice at the Reef's Edge
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, climax. Lena delivers the ledger to the harbor magistrate and the surviving sailors' families herself, standing between the crew and the owners' hired men. She names Hale's true story aloud — her guilt, her innocence, both. Beat: she chooses truth over the memory she was hiding inside.

chapters.title: After the Monsoon
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. The fallout: the owners fall, the fleet survives on honest charter work, Rennard sails away unpaid and unrepentant. Isolde tears up the old contract and offers Lena a new one — partnership, no debts. Beat: quiet reckoning; the crew, once strangers, is a family.

chapters.title: Years, Not Miles
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena stands on the reef coast at the start of the dry season, no longer measuring her life in distance. She keeps Hale's letter, visits his grave with the truth finally told, and signs Isolde's contract. Beat: resolution — loyalty rebuilt on truth, survival that cost something and was worth it.
